newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stocks end mixed even as CANTV soars.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stocks end mixed even as CANTV soars.

text.p: Caracas shares closed mixed in strong trade, even as newly issued stock in Venezuelan telephone company CANTV soared, traders said.
The bolsa's 19-share index gained 0.77 percent to close at 6,212.64 points, as a total of 25.5 million shares worth five billion bolivars ($10.6 million) changed hands.
CANTV closed up 12 percent on the day at 1727.00 bolivars ($3.67) as, among traded issues, 18 rose, 15 fell and seven closed flat.

"CANTV reminded me of the Peter and the Wolf story," said one trader. "An expectant market rose ahead of the placement, but didn't when the stock finally arrived," he said, adding "although it could do any moment."
Traders said an otherwise successful placement was only marred by a complicated system that allowed investors to move only 20 percent of their allotted CANTV stock.
Trade was originally slated to begin December 2, after first opening on the New York Stock Exchange. "Truthfully the market was fully prepared to begin today," said Financorp broker Edwin Escalona.
Over 73 million CANTV shares were sold to Venezuelan investors as some 34 million American Depository Receipts were simultaneously sold abroad. Each ADR represents seven Class B shares.

The share-offering -- one of the largest to come out of Latin America this year -- is expected to boost Venezuela's weighting among Latin American fund portfolios and attract foreign interest to Venezuelan equities generally.
Investors have viewed the sale as a crucial test of the government's commitment to tough economic reforms.

Among widely-held shares, Electricidad de Caracas slipped 9.50 bolivars to end at 540.00 bolivars, Sivensa lost 8.00 bolivars to finish at 352.00 bolivars and Mavesa gained 1.50 bolivars to close at 151.50 bolivars.
